A directed SQL Graph pattern uses arrows to specify the traversal direction. The pattern `p1-(k1)->p2-(k2)->p3` traverses exactly two directed `Knows` edges from the starting node `p1` to `p3`; filtering `p1.PersonID` by `@StartPersonId` establishes the origin, and selecting `p3.PersonID` and `p3.DisplayName` returns the people reached after the second relationship. Microsoft documents that MATCH patterns traverse from one node to another through an edge in the arrow’s specified direction.

**Learn more:** [MATCH (Transact-SQL) - SQL Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/sql/t-sql/queries/match-sql-graph?view=sql-server-ver16)

You have an Azure SQL database that includes a column named `Notes`.  
  
A security review finds that `Notes` contains sensitive data. You need to protect the data so that neither stored values nor query inputs disclose information about the actual data. The solution must prevent a user from inferring data relationships or repetitions from the encrypted output.  
  
Which should you use?
questions.explanation:
Always Encrypted with randomized encryption encrypts values and query parameters outside the database, and encrypts each occurrence of identical plaintext differently. This prevents encrypted output from revealing equality, repeated values, or relationships between plaintext values. Deterministic encryption intentionally produces matching ciphertext for matching plaintext and can therefore expose such patterns.

**Learn more:** [Always Encrypted cryptography - SQL Server | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/security/encryption/always-encrypted-cryptography?view=sql-server-ver17) · [Always Encrypted - SQL Server | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/security/encryption/always-encrypted-database-engine?view=azuresqldb-mi-current)

A reporting query that aggregates monthly revenue for each customer runs frequently. You need to reduce the time required to retrieve the computed values. The solution must **not** change any underlying table structure.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a view by using ORDER BY without TOP, and then create a unique clustered index on the view.
Create a view without using WITH SCHEMABINDING, and then create a nonclustered index on the view.
Create a view by using GROUP BY, and then create a unique clustered index on the view.
Create a view by using WITH SCHEMABINDING, include COUNT_BIG(*), and then create a unique clustered index on the view.

questions.explanation:
An indexed view materializes the aggregation in a unique clustered index, which can reduce repeated computation of monthly revenue per customer. For an indexed view, the view must use `WITH SCHEMABINDING`; when its definition uses `GROUP BY`, it must also include `COUNT_BIG(*)`. The unique clustered index is the initial index required to materialize the view.

**Learn more:** [Create indexed views - SQL Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/views/create-indexed-views?view=sql-server-ver17) · [CREATE INDEX (Transact-SQL)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/create-index-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17)

You use `AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS` and `VECTOR_SEARCH` to enable semantic search and apply additional filters to two columns named `Category` and `Price`.  
  
You plan to change the embedding model from `text-embedding-ada-002` to `text-embedding-3-small`. Existing rows already have embeddings in the `Embedding` column.  
  
You need to implement the model change. Applications must be able to use `VECTOR_SEARCH` without runtime errors.

Normalize the vector lengths before storing new embeddings.
Convert the Embedding column to nvarchar(max).
Create a vector index on dbo.Products.Embedding.

questions.explanation:
All persisted document embeddings must be regenerated with `text-embedding-3-small` before applications query with embeddings generated by that model. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a SQL database in Microsoft Fabric that includes a column named `Payload`. `Payload` stores customer data in JSON documents in the following format.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783922359795-hg5sfcuf.png)  
  
Data analysis indicates that some customers use subaddressing in their email addresses, for example, `user+tag@contoso.com`.  
  
You need to return a normalized email value that removes the subaddressing; for example, `user1+tag@contoso.com` must be normalized to `user1@contoso.com`.  
  
Which Transact-SQL expression should you use?
questions.explanation:
`REGEXP_REPLACE` replaces text that matches a regular-expression pattern. The pattern `\+.*@` matches the plus sign, the subaddressing text, and the following at sign. Replacing that match with `@` preserves the original local part and domain while removing the subaddressing.

**Learn more:** [REGEXP_REPLACE (Transact-SQL)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/functions/regexp-replace-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a SQL database in Microsoft Fabric containing an `nvarchar(max)` column named `MessageText`. An ID is always present within the first paragraph of `MessageText`.  
  
You need to write a Transact-SQL query using `REGEXP_SUBSTR` to extract the ID from `MessageText`.  
  
What should you include in the query?

options.text: Cast MessageText to nvarchar (4000) before calling REGEXP_SUBSTR.
Add a COLLATE Latin1_General_CS_AS clause to MessageText before calling REGEXP_SUBSTR.
Run TRY_CONVERT(varchar(max), MessageText) before calling REGEXP_SUBSTR.

questions.explanation:
In SQL Server 2025 / SQL database in Microsoft Fabric, the regular-expression functions have an important restriction: LOB types (varchar(max) and nvarchar(max), up to 2 MB) are supported only by REGEXP_LIKE, REGEXP_COUNT, and REGEXP_INSTR. REGEXP_SUBSTR, REGEXP_REPLACE, REGEXP_MATCHES, and REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE do NOT accept LOB input. Because MessageText is nvarchar(max), you must first cast it to a non-LOB type such as nvarchar(4000) before calling REGEXP_SUBSTR, which is fine here since the ID always appears in the first paragraph (choice B). A case-sensitive COLLATE clause (C) changes matching behavior but does not remove the LOB restriction, TRY_CONVERT to varchar(max) (D) is still a LOB, and STRING_ESCAPE (A) is unrelated.

**Learn more:** [REGEXP_SUBSTR (Transact-SQL)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/functions/regexp-substr-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17) · [Work with regular expressions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/regular-expressions/overview?view=azuresqldb-current)

SQL Server 2025 can run text-embedding inference locally by creating an external model configured for ONNX Runtime with local model and runtime paths, which does not require outbound connectivity. You have an Azure SQL database named AdventureWorksDB that includes a table named dbo.Employee.  
  
You have a C# Azure Functions app that uses an HTTP-triggered function and an Azure SQL input binding to query dbo.Employee.  
  
You are adding a second function that responds to row changes in dbo.Employee and writes structured logs.  
  
You need to configure AdventureWorksDB and the app to meet these requirements:  
  
- Changes to dbo.Employee must invoke the new function within five seconds.  
- Each invocation must handle no more than 100 changes.  
  
Which two database configurations should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Create an AFTER trigger on dbo.Employee for Data Manipulation Language (DML).
Enable change tracking on the dbo.Employee table.
Enable change tracking at the database level.
Enable change data capture (CDC) for dbo.Employee table changes.

questions.explanation:
The Azure SQL trigger binding uses SQL change tracking to detect row inserts, updates, and deletes. Change tracking must be enabled both for the database and for the specific monitored table. The trigger’s default maximum batch size is 100 changes and its default polling interval is 1,000 milliseconds, satisfying the stated limits without requiring a database configuration change. [Azure SQL trigger for Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-azure-sql-trigger)

**Learn more:** [Azure SQL trigger for Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-azure-sql-trigger)

You have an Azure SQL database that contains database-level Data Definition Language (DDL) triggers, including one named `ddl_Audit`.  
  
You need to stop `ddl_Audit` from firing during the next deployment while keeping the trigger object in place.  
  
Which Transact-SQL statement should you use?
questions.explanation:
`DISABLE TRIGGER` prevents a database-scoped DDL trigger from firing without dropping the trigger object. For this trigger, the applicable form is `DISABLE TRIGGER ddl_Audit ON DATABASE`.\

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783921989609-g8qa729y.png)  
  
What should you insert at line 22?

`FOR JSON PATH, WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPER` serializes the outer `SELECT` as one JSON object for the chat-completions request body. `FOR JSON PATH` maps the `messages[0]` and `messages[1]` aliases to nested JSON properties, and `WITHOUT_ARRAY_WRAPPER` prevents a top-level array. `JSON_QUERY(@chunks)` preserves the retrieved chunks as an embedded JSON fragment rather than escaped text.

`TRUNCATE TABLE` with the `PARTITIONS` clause removes data from the specified partition without logging individual row deletions. Truncating only the oldest monthly partition targets the required data-retention slice and uses fewer transaction-log and locking resources than deleting its rows individually. The table and its indexes must be aligned to use partition truncation.

**Learn more:** [TRUNCATE TABLE (Transact-SQL)](https://learn.microsoft.com/mt-mt/sql/t-sql/statements/truncate-table-transact-sql?view=sql-server-linux-ver16) · [Partitioned tables and indexes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/partitions/partitioned-tables-and-indexes?view=sql-server-ver17)

Solution: Execute the following Transact-SQL statement.  
  
```sql  
DELETE FROM dbo.Orders -  
WHERE OrderDate < DATEADD(month, -36, SYSUTCDATETIME());  
```  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation: A row-by-row DELETE is not a low-impact way to remove an entire monthly partition from a large partitioned table. It can consume transaction-log and processing resources and interfere with concurrent access; removing data through a partition-level approach is needed to minimize impact on other queries.

questions.domain: Design and develop database solutions
questions.question:
Solution: Determine the partition scheme for the oldest month, then execute the following Transact-SQL statement.  
  
```sql  
ALTER TABLE dbo.Orders -  
DROP PARTITION SCHEME (partition_scheme_name);  
```  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
`DROP PARTITION SCHEME` is a standalone Transact-SQL statement, not an `ALTER TABLE` operation, and a partition scheme cannot be dropped while a table or index uses it. Dropping the scheme would not selectively remove the oldest monthly partition from `dbo.Orders`. [Microsoft Learn: DROP PARTITION SCHEME (Transact-SQL)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/drop-partition-scheme-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17)\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure SQL database that supports the OLTP workload for an order-processing application.  
  
During a 10-minute incident window, you run a dynamic management view query and find the following:  
  
- Session 72 is sleeping with `open_transaction_count = 1`.  
- Multiple other sessions display `blocking_session_id = 72` in `sys.dm_exec_requests`.  
- `sys.dm_exec_input_buffer(72, NULL)` returns only `BEGIN TRANSACTION UPDATE Sales.Orders`.  
- Users report that updates to `Sales.Orders` intermittently time out during the incident window.  
- The timeouts stop only after you manually terminate session 72.  
  
What could be causing the blocking?

options.text: A long-running SELECT statement is blocking writers.
An explicit transaction was started but not committed or rolled back.

questions.explanation:
An explicit transaction begun with `BEGIN TRANSACTION` remains active until `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK`. Locks acquired by the `UPDATE Sales.Orders` can therefore remain held while the session is sleeping, blocking conflicting updates until the transaction is ended or the session is terminated.

**Learn more:** [Understand and Resolve Blocking Problems - Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/understand-resolve-blocking?view=azuresql) · [BEGIN TRANSACTION (Transact-SQL)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/language-elements/begin-transaction-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure SQL database containing tables named `dbo.ProductDocs` and `dbo.ProductDocsEmbeddings`. `dbo.ProductDocs` stores product documentation and has these columns:  
  
- `DocID` (`int`)  
- `Title` (`nvarchar(200)`)  
- `Body` (`nvarchar(max)`)  
- `LastModified` (`datetime2`)  
  
The documentation is edited throughout the day.  
  
`dbo.ProductDocsEmbeddings` has the following columns:  
  
- `DocID` (`int`)  
- `ChunkOrder` (`int`)  
- `ChunkText` (`nvarchar(max)`)  
- `Embedding` (`vector(1536)`)  
  
The current embedding pipeline runs once each night.  
  
You need to ensure embeddings are updated whenever the underlying documentation content changes. The solution must **not** require a nightly batch process.  
  
What should you include in the solution?
questions.explanation:
Azure SQL change tracking records committed DML changes for enabled tables and lets an application retrieve the rows that changed and then read their current values. An incremental embedding process can use those changes to regenerate the affected chunks and vectors as documentation is edited, rather than relying on a nightly batch. Microsoft Learn describes change tracking as a lightweight mechanism for identifying changed rows and obtaining their latest data from the tracked table.

**Learn more:** [About Change Tracking (SQL Server)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/track-changes/about-change-tracking-sql-server?view=sql-server-ver17) · [Track Data Changes (SQL Server)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/track-changes/track-data-changes-sql-server?view=sql-server-ver17)

DB1 has tables that store sensitive customer data.  
  
You need to ensure that every Transact-SQL query executed from GitHub Copilot Chat in SSMS is constrained by the same permissions as the developer’s database login.  
  
What stops GitHub Copilot Chat-executed queries from accessing data beyond the developer’s authorized access?

options.text: GitHub Copilot Chat runs queries in a read-only sandbox that is isolated from production database permissions.
GitHub Copilot Chat runs queries by using the developer’s database identity and permissions.
GitHub Copilot Chat filters query results on the client side to remove rows the developer is unauthorized to see.
GitHub Copilot Chat uses different row-level security (RLS) policies than the developer.

questions.explanation:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure SQL database named ProductsDB.  
  
You deploy Data API builder (DAB) to Azure Container Apps by using the `mcr.microsoft.com/azure-databases/data-api-builder:latest` image.  
  
The container app has these configurations:  
  
- **Secrets:** `mssql-connection-string`, `dab-config-base64`  
- **Environment variables:**  
  - `MSSQL_CONNECTION_STRING=secretref:mssql-connection-string`  
  - `DAB_CONFIG_BASE64=secretref:dab-config-base64`  
- **Ingress:** External on port 5000  
  
Users report that the `/health` endpoint returns a healthy response, but every request that queries an entity named Products fails and produces a connection error.  
  
You confirm that the SQL login in the connection string is correct and that the database exists.  
  
You need to ensure that the container app can establish connections to the Azure SQL logical server without changing the container app deployment settings or the DAB configuration file.  
  
What should you do on the Azure SQL logical server?

options.text: Create an auto-failover group for ProductsDB.
Create a firewall rule that allows a start and end IP address of 0.0.0.0.
Enable FORCE_LAST_GOOD_PLAN automatic tuning for ProductsDB.

questions.explanation:
Azure SQL Database requires its logical server firewall to allow connections from Azure-hosted resources. A server-level rule whose start and end IP addresses are both `0.0.0.0` enables Azure services and resources to pass through the firewall and attempt database connections. This is the network setting required for the container app to connect when its credentials and database are already valid.

**Learn more:** [IP Firewall Rules - Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/firewall-configure?view=azuresql-db) · [az sql server firewall-rule](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/sql/server/firewall-rule?view=azure-cli-latest)

A deployment pipeline may be automatically rerun after a transient failure.  
  
You need to deploy the reference data as part of the same CI/CD process. Rerunning the pipeline must yield the same result and must **not** create duplicate rows.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add a post-deployment script that inserts reference rows by using IF NOT EXISTS or MERGE logic.
Restore a backup after each deployment.
Store the reference values in GitHub repository secrets.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You plan to update `sp_UpdateProcedureForPatient` to satisfy the performance requirements by running all of its code within a transaction.  
  
Which transaction isolation level should you use?

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784704107157-xwcbfs9m.png)

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784704110883-rv2frunl.png)
questions.explanation:
`REPEATABLE READ` prevents other transactions from modifying rows read by the current transaction until that transaction completes. This meets the requirement that records accessed by the procedure must not be changed while it runs. `SERIALIZABLE` also prevents phantom inserts into qualifying key ranges, which is not required here.

**Learn more:** [SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL (Transact-SQL)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/set-transaction-isolation-level-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17)

Create a vector index on products.embedding and change the query to use VECTOR_SEARCH and METRIC = ‘cosine’.
Add a nonclustered index on products.embedding.

questions.explanation:
`VECTOR_DISTANCE` calculates exact vector distances and does not use a vector index, which can require comparisons across all embeddings. A vector index combined with `VECTOR_SEARCH` enables approximate nearest-neighbor search, reducing the work required for semantic search. The vector index must match the search metric, so the cosine metric should be used for both the index and `VECTOR_SEARCH`.

WHERE CAST(CreateDate AS date) = @0rderDate.

You need to enhance data-retrieval performance and decrease the number of tokens used for each retrieval.  
  
What should you implement?
questions.explanation:
Chunking splits source documents into smaller, relevant passages that can be independently indexed and retrieved for a RAG workflow. Returning focused passages instead of entire documents reduces the token context supplied to the model and avoids the latency and cost associated with processing oversized content.\
